title: Asia Society Texas Brings Diwali Lights Back to Houston on October 18
excerpt: The free, family-friendly festival of lights returns to the Texas Center in the Museum District on October 18, with food, fashion, crafts and a Ramayana performance — three weeks before Lakshmi Puja.
body:
• Asia Society Texas hosts its annual “Diwali Lights!” festival on Sunday, October 18, 2026, from 2:00 to 6:00 PM at the Texas Center, 1370 Southmore Blvd, Houston — free, with registration required.
  • The family-friendly festival features Indian fashion, food, diya painting, henna, rangoli, a shopping bazaar, and a ticketed Ramayana theater performance ($15; 35% off for members).
  • The 2025 edition sold out with more than 500 guests, cementing the event as an anchor of Houston’s Indian-American community calendar.
  • Held about three weeks before Lakshmi Puja on November 8, 2026, the festival is one of Houston’s earliest Diwali-season celebrations.

Asia Society Texas is throwing open its doors for Diwali season. The institution’s annual “Diwali Lights!” festival returns to the Asia Society Texas Center in Houston’s Museum District on Sunday, October 18, 2026, from 2:00 to 6:00 PM — a free, family-friendly celebration of the festival of lights with Indian fashion, food, hands-on activities, and a theatrical Ramayana performance.

“Celebrate one of the most cherished holidays in India and beyond: Diwali! This free, family-friendly festival of lights brings the spirit of the season to life with vibrant Indian fashion, delicious food, hands-on activities, and a captivating Ramayana performance.”

— Asia Society Texas

What to expect

If the 2025 edition is any guide, visitors are in for a packed afternoon. Last year’s sold-out festival drew more than 500 guests, with food from FiLLi Cafe, Madras Pavilion, Masala Munchies and It’s A Wrap Food Truck, plus complimentary Diwali sundaes from Gallivant Ice Cream — which returns this year. Activities included diya painting, henna, carrom, rangoli, block printing, and a Diwali art contest, alongside a shopping bazaar featuring Designs by Sippy, Disha Thadani and the Eternal Gandhi Museum Houston.

The performing arts lineup has been a signature of the event. In 2025, the Houston Music Festival presented “This City, Our Stories,” and Rathna Kumar with Indian Performing Arts Samskriti staged “The Ramayan Project,” a cross-cultural production weaving together the music and dance traditions of India, Indonesia and Sri Lanka. This year’s Ramayana theater performance is ticketed at $15, with a 35% discount for Asia Society Texas members.

Houston’s Diwali anchor

Asia Society Texas — at 1370 Southmore Blvd — is the city’s flagship Asian cultural institution, and its Diwali celebration has become an annual anchor of the community calendar. Houston is one of America’s most diverse metros and home to a large, established Indian-American community, from the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Stafford to the Eternal Gandhi Museum. The sponsors’ list for the festival reads like a who’s who of Houston’s Indian philanthropy, including Anil Aggarwal, Sushila and Durga Agrawal, and the Hari and Anjali Agrawal Charitable Foundation.

Asia Society says its mission is to “advance cultural exchange by celebrating the vibrant diversity of Asia, inspiring empathy, and fostering a better understanding of our interconnected world” — and Diwali, observed by Hindus, Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists as the triumph of light over darkness, is the marquee moment for that mission.

Three weeks before the big night

Diwali 2026’s main night — Lakshmi Puja — falls on Sunday, November 8, so the October 18 festival is a pre-Diwali kickoff, one of Houston’s earliest community celebrations of the season. For families looking to mark the festival of lights before the actual holiday week, the Texas Center’s free afternoon of food, craft and performance is the easiest entry point on the calendar.
nri_angle: Houston’s large Indian-American community gets one of its earliest Diwali-season celebrations of 2026 at Asia Society Texas’s free “Diwali Lights!” festival on October 18.
